shipped_originals.title_o: Run for the team: An analysis of effort gains in track and field relays

blind_target.evidence_quote: In a replication and extension of this study, we wanted to find out whether its findings replicate in a sample of 1,718 observations from 1,270 U.S. college athletes and whether effort expenditure is driven by working in a team or the chance of valuable outcomes in the relay.
blind_target.outcome_quote: As shown by linear mixed modeling and regression analyses, runners exhibited effort gains only if their relays had high medal chances and if they had not been successful in the individual competition (i.e., did not place first to third). Moreover, relay members who had been successful in the individual competition showed effort losses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original effort gains are stated and the replication finds them only under restricted conditions, with losses in others; provisionally mixed. Complete reference entry is not present in the saved abstract; no citation metadata guessed.

blind_target.title: When Efortful Thinking Influences Judgmental Anchoring: Differential Effects of Forewarning and Incentives on Self-generated and Externally Provided Anchors
blind_target.evidence_quote:
In their Study 2, Epley and Gilovich (2005) found that warning participants that their adjustments
from anchors were insufficient led to increases in adjustments from self-generated anchors but not
from experimenter-provided anchors. We conducted a preregistered (https://osf.io/f5sj8) replica-
tion of this study.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Thus, we deem
the replication an informative failure: There is evidence against the hypothesis that forewarning
moderates adjustment from self-generated anchors.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The moderators forming the central finding did not replicate. General anchoring effects are checks of the paradigm, not a successful replication of the moderator claim.

corrected_value.title: When Efortful Thinking Influences Judgmental Anchoring: Differential Effects of Forewarning and Incentives on Self-generated and Externally Provided Anchors

prior_decision.quote: Study 3 is a replication of Epley and Gilovich (2005, Study 2) and investigated the moderator forewarning.
prior_decision.reason: In Study 3, the paper conducts a preregistered replication of a separate original article, Epley and Gilovich (2005, Study 2; DOI: 10.1002/bdm.495), which is an omitted target in the shipped dataset and resulted in a failed replication.

shipped_originals.title_o: Human Fallibility and Learning from Errors at Work

blind_target.title: Modelling learning from errors in daily work.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The goal of our study was to investigate whether exploratory findings from an earlier study on hospital nurses’ ESLA (Bauer and Mulder Learning in Health and Social Care 6:121–133, 2011) replicate and generalise to the domain of elder care nursing.
blind_target.outcome_quote: These results entirely cross-validate the exploratory findings of Bauer and Mulder (Learning in Health and Social Care 6:121–133, 2011) on hospital nurses’ ESLA and show that they generalise to the domain of elder care nursing.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly say the results entirely cross-validate the earlier exploratory findings.

shipped_originals.title_o: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice

blind_target.title: Experimental investigation of the subjective value of information in trading.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The current research is closest to a set of studies in information science conducted by Rafaeli and Raban (27, 28), who replicated the endowment effect for information in a game mimicking sales decisions. They gave participants the opportunity to buy and sell information, and observed greater willingness-to-accept prices than willingness-to-pay amounts. We extend their work in several critical ways.
blind_target.outcome_quote: However, we predicted that participants endowed with the three-fact bundle would be less likely than nonendowed participants to choose the four-fact bundle, because doing so would feel to them like a loss—rather than foregone gain—of three facts. Indeed, participants in the endowed condition were more likely to prefer learning just three facts (68%) than those in the nonendowed condition (46%) (χ2(1, n = 146) = 7.03, P = 0.008, Φ = 0.219) (Fig. 2).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly extends the cited information-endowment experiments, addressing their monetary and instrumental confounds. Study 2 finds the predicted ownership preference in noninstrumental information, agreeing with their endowment finding. Target relation is conceptual and somewhat less explicit than the Asian Disease target.
